thesis: This is a big-mana Dinosaur deck with two engines that share a board: an eight-mana commander who converts combat damage into free Dinosaurs off the top of the library, and a four-mana Human who converts a Dinosaur entering into one damage to everything, which four enrage bodies plus Wrathful Raptors then turn into cards, tokens, lands and exile — and the second engine is the one that is actually online, because goldfish never casts the first one by turn 10 in 55% of games.

stages.label: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-seven entries whose whole job is an eight-drop, and the most reliable class in the deck: 'Ramp or fixing drawn' is 14 cards, 66.8% of opening sevens, 93.9% assembled, 86.9% by turn 6, mean turn 2.044. It still does not get there. Goldfish puts the commander's mean cast turn at 7.969, median 8, 8.3% by turn 6, and 5,533 of 10,000 iterations never cast him by turn 10 — a conservative bound, since the simulation models no cost reduction at all. Two pressures pull apart here. Land drops hold at 89.4% on turn 3 and fall to 52.6% by turn 6, so the back half of the climb rides five rocks — one of them Mirari's Wake, a land-doubler rather than a rock in play terms — and three dorks rather than lands. And the strain is COLOUR, not quantity: 48 mana sources against Burgess' 42, but colour totals of G26/R20/W20 against a 36-source yardstick, with Wakening Sun's Avatar asking WWW off twenty white. Two traps, and the second needs its WHOLE clause read. Unclaimed Territory's restricted mana is spells-only. Secluded Courtyard's adds 'or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type' — and Belbe's Portal is an Artifact, Monster Manual an Artifact — Book, so neither land's coloured mana pays those activations either. What pays there is each land's plain '{T}: Add {C}' against the Portal's generic {3} and the Manual's {1}, with the Manual's {G} coming from elsewhere. Courtyard is still the better land named on Dinosaur: it pays Zacama's {2}{R}/{2}{G}/{2}{W} and Bronzebeak Foragers' {X}{W}, which ARE creature sources of the chosen type. Rogue's Passage and Kessig Wolf Run are lands and are deliberately NOT here: in this deck their job is getting seven damage through, and they are filed under ignition.

stages.label: TWO IGNITIONS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME PRICE
stages.what_it_does: The deck has two first windows and they cost 8 mana and 4 mana. THE HEADLINE: Gishath resolves and deals combat damage to a player, revealing that many cards and free-rolling every Dinosaur among them (stack 001). 'Vigilance, trample, haste' is PRINTED on him, so haste is not what he needs; he needs to CONNECT. Trample means a chump block only shrinks the reveal, Rogue's Passage guarantees all seven, Kessig Wolf Run makes it more. Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator are the only cards in the 99 that make a COMMAND-ZONE cast cheaper ({1} off Dinosaur spells, {2} off the chosen type); Regisaur Alpha's haste is for the Dinosaurs that arrive, not for the 7/6. THE CHEAP ONE: Forerunner of the Empire, four mana, 'whenever a Dinosaur you control enters, you may have this creature deal 1 damage to each creature' — optional, free, repeatable, and the only such source in the deck (stacks 003 and 005 are both ignited by it). Its ETB also puts a Dinosaur on top of the library — the commander's reveal, pre-loaded. Itzquinth is NOT a cheap version of it: two mana, no tutor, an ETB reading 'you may pay {2}. When you do, target Dinosaur you control deals damage equal to its power to another target creature' — one target, one enrage payoff at most, at that Dinosaur's power, so aiming a Polyraptor at your own board is 5 into a 5/5. It is here because a Dinosaur ENTERING puts Forerunner's trigger on the stack — its whole contribution in stack 005. Forerunner, not the commander, is the single point of failure: Gishath returns from the command zone at tax, Forerunner does not, and it is a Human Soldier outside every tribal protection layer here.

stages.label: WHAT THE REVEAL IS MADE OF
cards: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People
stages.what_it_does: The cascade eats the top of the library, so the fuel is density plus stacking. Density is structural: 29 of the deck's 34 creature copies are Dinosaurs, and the five that are not include Forerunner itself, so the trigger can never free-roll the enrage web's own damage source. Stacking is deliberate — Congregation at Dawn puts three creature cards on top at INSTANT speed, which is the reveal pre-loaded rather than a tutor; Worldly Tutor does one; Enlightened Tutor finds Urza's Incubator, Garruk's Uprising or Descendants' Path. The other half of this stage skips the commander entirely: Descendants' Path REVEALS the top card each upkeep and lets you cast it free only if it is a creature sharing a type with a creature you already control — otherwise it goes to the bottom, so it is a coin flipped once a turn, gated on the board the deck is trying to establish; Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual put one from HAND onto the battlefield, and Huatli's Roar chapter III searches a Dinosaur to hand. That matters for how the declaration reads: all four sit in the 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' target (6 cards, 67.3% assembled, 56.2% by turn 6), and none of the four can reach the command zone — but the target's other two members, Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator, are the command-zone discounts ignition names. The rate therefore fires on a body arriving OR on a cheaper commander and cannot say which; proposed_goldfish_edits[0] asks for that split. Bonehoard Dracosaur, Etali, Hunter's Insight and Rishkar's Expertise are the refills; three of the five cards with no entry in card_roles.json at all (Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Rishkar's Expertise) are in this stage, which is why the card-advantage axis under-reads.

stages.label: TWO TRIGGER CONDITIONS, TEN PAYOFFS
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper, and it runs on two conditions. (A) SOMETHING ENTERS: Pantlaza discovers X equal to the entering Dinosaur's toughness; Garruk's Uprising and Vaultborn Tyrant share a power-4 gate — Uprising draws, Vaultborn gains 3 and draws, and stack 001's 3/3 Regisaur token misses BOTH. Declared 'Dinosaur payoff', 7 cards, 73.7% assembled, 62.3% by turn 6 — members that are not interchangeable: only Pantlaza and Forerunner of the Empire trigger on EACH Dinosaur entry, and PANTLAZA is the rationed one — stack 001 puts four of its triggers on the stack for one discover, while Forerunner's ping has no rider. Curious Altisaur and Quartzwood Crasher want combat damage to a player. (B) A DINOSAUR IS DEALT DAMAGE. Four carry Enrage: Ripjaw draws, Polyraptor copies itself, Ranging Raptors fetches a basic, Trapjaw Tyrant exiles an opponent's creature. Wrathful Raptors is NOT one of them — it triggers on ANY Dinosaur you control taking damage and throws that much at a non-Dinosaur target, which is how four damaged Dinosaurs, three at 1 and a dying Temple Altisaur at 13, became 16 points in stack 004. Declared at 5 cards, 60.8% assembled, 50.6% by turn 6, mean turn 3.053; stack 005 turns one optional ping into four enrage triggers, five payoffs banked and every creature of yours surviving. THERE IS NO FODDER STAGE, and that is the point of enrage: the resource converted is damage marked on your own board — no card, cleared at cleanup. The exceptions are priced elsewhere: Temple Altisaur dies to the sweeper in stack 004, Forerunner to its own third sweep in stack 003, which bounds the Polyraptor loop at seven — the real price of no fodder stage, since the maximum line pays for the board with ignition's single point of failure.

stages.label: ANSWERS, AND A SECOND PING
stages.what_it_does: Eleven cards, and the least typal thing about the deck: 11 removal copies in an 18-card interactive suite, two sweepers, five permanent classes with nothing uncovered — though graveyard rests on Intrepid Paleontologist alone and land on Beast Within alone, so the coverage is thin, not surplus. Exactly ONE sweeper spares your side, and only conditionally: Wakening Sun's Avatar destroys all non-Dinosaur creatures only 'if you cast it from your hand', so a copy delivered by the commander's trigger, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual or Descendants' Path is a vanilla 7/7, which makes the WWW off twenty white sources a requirement, not a preference. Austere Command does NOT: its creature modes read mana value 3 or less and 4 or greater, neither reads Dinosaur, and the deck's 34 creature copies split 11 against 23 — either mode takes a third or two thirds of your own board. Blasphemous Act, made one-sided by Temple Altisaur in protection, is the one single point of failure deck-audit priced here, doing two jobs: a 13-point wipe costing {R} off nine creatures, and the largest self-damage source the enrage web has. Stack 004 resolves it end to end and bounds it: all five opposing creatures die to state-based actions BEFORE the redirect targets are chosen (the stack's 'six lethally-damaged creatures' counts your own Temple Altisaur), and the four Wrathful triggers total 16 at one seat, taking that opponent from 26 to 10 and leaving the other at 31. That dual role is why an arrow runs BACKWARD from here into conversion: three more cards point damage at your own board (Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur's {2}{R} discard mode, Zacama's {2}{R}), making the removal suite a second ignition for the enrage web when Forerunner is not on the table.

stages.label: INSURANCE, AND ONE PREVENTION SHIELD
stages.what_it_does: Six cards, and the declared group measures only five of them: 'Protection held for the board' is the five instants at 59.0% assembled, 48.5% by turn 6, and Temple Altisaur is not in it. Read the five instants rather than counting them. Heroic Intervention's hexproof and Akroma's Will's protection from each colour answer targeted exile and bounce, so the class is broader than indestructible; Eerie Interlude is the only member that dodges a non-targeted mass exile; and Flawless Maneuver is the only one castable for nothing, which is the whole argument for it, because on the turn you tap out for an eight-drop it is the only shield you can hold up. A second duty nobody declares: the board-wide instants are the only cards that cover Forerunner of the Empire, a Human Soldier standing outside every tribal layer here. Temple Altisaur is the sixth and is not an enrage payoff — it is a static prevention effect ('prevent all but 1' of any damage to ANOTHER Dinosaur you control) and it is what turns a symmetrical 13-point wipe into a one-sided one. Stack 004 prices what that costs: Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, eats the unprevented 13 and dies. Named as this stage's single point of failure because the pair with Blasphemous Act is two named singletons and the LOWEST-measured target on the deck — 2.5% assembled, 1.4% by turn 6, mean turn 5.462, each half 7.1% of an opening seven.

stages.label: ONE SWING, AND NOBODY HAS MEASURED IT
stages.what_it_does: The game ends in combat, with a board the other six stages built. Overwhelming Stampede is the alpha strike — trample plus +X/+X where X is your greatest power, which on a cascade board is a 7/6 commander or a 12/12 — and Garruk's Uprising has already given the whole team trample from the conversion stage. Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs {X} less for the total power of your creatures, so a cascade board casts a 12/12 for {G}{G}; Ghalta and Mavren converts an attack into a tapped-and-attacking X/X or a row of lifelinking Vampires; Regal Imperiosaur is a flat +1/+1 anthem for the other Dinosaurs; Carnage Tyrant is the one threat that beats both a counterspell and targeted removal. Pugnacious Hammerskull is the weakest card in the stage and is honest about it — a 6/6 for {2}{G} that stun-counters itself whenever it attacks while you control no other Dinosaur, which is a card asking you to already have the board it is meant to build. THE GAP WORTH STATING: none of the five checker-passed stacks resolves a kill. They resolve a cascade, two enrage webs, a bounded token loop and a sweeper explicitly measured as NOT lethal (16 redirected damage taking one opponent from 26 to 10). There is exactly ONE arrow into this stage — conversion to wincon, Polyraptor plus Overwhelming Stampede — and it is dashed, as is the single arrow back out, and the lethal threshold this deck actually needs is an open question rather than a figure.

map_disagreements.why: engine-facts reports 2 of 8 components sitting in a single city, and BOTH of those are the size-1 halves of the Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur target — a one-card component is coherent by arithmetic. Not one component with more than one card is coherent on this deck, which is the strongest statement of the map-versus-engine gap in the fleet so far.

four of the five bodies here carry Enrage and share one trigger CONDITION ('whenever this creature is dealt damage'); the fifth, Wrathful Raptors, reads 'whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage' instead, so all five key off the same event on your board and differ entirely in EFFECT — and the map reads effects. Ranging Raptors says 'search your library for a basic land' so it clusters with the ramp spells; Trapjaw Tyrant says 'exile target creature an opponent controls' so it clusters with the removal. The condition is the engine and it is the part of the card the clustering cannot see.

four cities for eight cards, because the connection kit is defined by a requirement printed on ONE card. Nothing on Rogue's Passage says Gishath and nothing on Gishath says 'needs a land'. Forerunner of the Empire lands in THE SEARCH PARTY on its ETB tutor clause, which is the half of the card that is not the engine — the half that is, 'you may have this creature deal 1 damage to each creature', is what two passing stacks are about.

the four protection instants sit together in THE PIVOT TURN and the fifth shield does not, because Temple Altisaur is a 5-mana 3/4 Dinosaur whose text is a static prevention clause with no protection vocabulary in it. It clusters with the creatures it protects. Same shape as Eerie Interlude, which the taxonomy tags 'recursion' and the map files with the Dinosaurs it blinks.

the declared 14-card ramp class spans five cities and the stage spans the same five, because 'produces mana' is not a thing cards say — they say 'search your library' (the land-ramp spells), '{T}: Add' (the rocks), or nothing at all (the 22 plain lands). BUYING TURNS is the one city this stage contains whole, and it is five artifacts.

open_questions.question: What rate does the enrage web ACTUALLY assemble at — a self-damage source AND a converter in the same game? goldfish_targets.json declares the five converters ('Enrage engine drawn', 60.8% assembled, 50.6% by turn 6) and declares no source at all, so the measured number describes five payoffs with nothing to ping them.
open_questions.why_it_matters: conversion is the deck's real engine and the one that is online before turn 8. A rate that counts converters alone will read as healthy in exactly the games where the web never fires.

open_questions.question: What board actually kills a 40-life opponent here, and from how far? No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing; the closest measurement is stack 004's 16 redirected damage taking one opponent from 26 to 10, explicitly not lethal.
open_questions.why_it_matters: every arrow into wincon is currently dashed, and the Game Plan department will otherwise state a kill the evidence tier does not carry. Radagast's finisher needed the threshold proved from both sides — a floor that loses and a board that is exactly lethal.

open_questions.why_it_matters: the entire ignition stage is priced off that number, and the difference between 'the commander is a turn-8 play' and 'the commander is unreachable' is the difference between two different decks.

If it's a creature card that SHARES A CREATURE TYPE WITH A CREATURE YOU CONTROL, you MAY cast it without paying its mana cost. If you don't cast it, put it on the bottom.' findings.where: stages[1].what_it_does (ignition), 'Itzquinth is the one-shot version at two mana'
findings.claim: Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath is a one-shot Forerunner of the Empire
findings.note: It is neither half of Forerunner. Forerunner's engine clause deals '1 damage to EACH creature' -- that is what fires five payoffs at once in 005 -- and its ETB tutors a Dinosaur to the top. Itzquinth's oracle is 'Haste / When Itzquinth enters, you may pay {2}. When you do, TARGET Dinosaur you control deals damage equal to its power to ANOTHER TARGET CREATURE.' Single target, no tutor, and it needs a second creature to point at. It can fire at most one enrage payoff, and pointing it at your own Polyraptor is a 5-damage hit on a 5/5. In stack 005 Itzquinth's own ability is never used: the resolution says it 'contributes nothing beyond having triggered the ping by entering'. Its listing in proposed_goldfish_edits[2]'s self-damage group is defensible -- it CAN damage your own Dinosaur -- but calling it the cheap Forerunner mis-sizes the deck's scarcest resource, and the ignition stage's own SPOF argument depends on Forerunner being 'the only such source in the deck', which the next sentence then contradicts.

findings.where: stages[4].what_it_does (output), 'Two sweepers spare your side by construction: Wakening Sun's Avatar destroys all NON-Dinosaur creatures'

findings.note: Its oracle is 'When this creature enters, IF YOU CAST IT FROM YOUR HAND, destroy all non-Dinosaur creatures.' In a model whose headline is a commander putting Dinosaur creature cards onto the battlefield from the library, that rider is load-bearing and is nowhere in the file: a Wakening Sun's Avatar delivered by Gishath's trigger, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual or Descendants' Path is a vanilla 7/7, not a sweeper. It also makes the WWW off twenty white sources (stages[0]) a hard requirement rather than a preference, because the free-roll routes cannot substitute for casting it. State the rider, or the Game Plan will count two sweepers the cascade cannot produce.

findings.claim: Two dashed lines written in the indicative with no hedge
findings.note: Four of the six dashed lines say so in their own note -- lines[0] 'this arrow is a claim', lines[5] 'no stack has resolved the two together', lines[6] 'claimed, not checked', lines[7] 'so this stays dashed'. lines[8] (wincon -> conversion) and lines[9] (protection -> ignition) do not: 'the second feedback loop: the alpha strike grants trample to everything...' and 'free with a commander, which is the only shield you can hold up...' are both flat assertions. Two substantive problems ride on that. (a) lines[8] conflates its two payoffs: Quartzwood Crasher needs 'creatures you control WITH TRAMPLE' dealing combat damage, Curious Altisaur triggers on any Dinosaur connecting and needs no trample at all -- and Curious Altisaur is not in the line's via. (b) lines[9]'s free cast is gated on 'if you control a commander', and goldfish puts the commander's mean cast at 7.969 with 5,533 of 10,000 games never casting him by turn 10. Forerunner is a four-drop that is live from turn 4-6. So in the majority of games, at exactly the window where Forerunner is the deck's only working ignition, Flawless Maneuver costs {2}{W} like any other trick and 'the only shield you can hold up' is false. That tension is the most interesting thing on this line and the note asserts past it.

findings.claim: Vaultborn Tyrant is a something-enters payoff
findings.note: Its trigger is 'Whenever this creature or another creature you control WITH POWER 4 OR GREATER enters, you gain 3 life and draw a card.' The same sentence states the gate for Garruk's Uprising ('draws on each power-4 body') and drops it for Vaultborn, which makes the two read as different breadths when they are the same. It matters against the model's own evidence: in stack 001 both Ravenous Sailback (power 3) and the 3/3 Regisaur token miss Uprising, and they would miss Vaultborn identically.

findings.where: thesis, 'which five enrage bodies then turn into cards, tokens, lands and exile'

findings.note: Four carry the Enrage keyword (Ripjaw Raptor, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant). Wrathful Raptors does not: 'Whenever a Dinosaur YOU CONTROL is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a Dinosaur' -- a board-wide damage-triggered payoff, not a self-enrage. The stage heading gets this right ('(B) A DINOSAUR IS DEALT DAMAGE'), and the distinction favours the deck: Wrathful converts damage dealt to Dinosaurs that have no enrage of their own, which is why it produced 16 points in 004 off three creatures that just take 1. Worth stating rather than flattening, since 'five enrage bodies' is the phrase the magazine will inherit.
